core_obligations: Let Y -> X be the finite etale Galois cover corresponding to Ker(rho); its automorphism group is Im(rho) and phi^*F_rho is the constant sheaf M_Y (proof lines 3447-3451). The push-pull trace map phi_*phi^*F_rho -> F_rho induces on H_c^2 the composite H_c^2(X_kbar, phi_*phi^*F_rho) = H_c^2(Y_kbar, M) = direct sum of M over the irreducible components of Y_kbar (proof lines 3453-3462). The set of irreducible components of Y_k is Im(rho) modulo the image of the geometric fundamental group (proof lines 3472-3475), so H_c^2(X_kbar, F_rho) is a quotient of the coinvariant module M_{pi_1(X_kbar)} (proof lines 3476-3478). Conversely the sheaf F_rho surjects onto the constant sheaf associated to the coinvariants, giving a map H_c^2(X_kbar, F_rho) -> M_{pi_1(X_kbar)} (proof lines 3479-3490). The Galois action carries the inverse cyclotomic character, because H_c^2(X_kbar, mu_n) is canonically Z/nZ (proof lines 3491-3492). Hence H_c^2(X_kbar, F_rho) = (M)_{pi_1(X_kbar)}(-1) (proof lines 3445-3492).
proof_roadmap: Trivialize F_rho on the Galois cover and compute H_c^2 of the constant sheaf via components (proof lines 3447-3467).
Identify the components with coinvariants and get both the quotient and the surjection; fix the twist via mu_n (proof lines 3472-3492).
